note: The manager owns this file. It is structured ON PURPOSE — the previous loop kept its state as a prose header, which degenerated into a 4,000-character run-on paragraph of abbreviations that no longer carried signal. Structure resists that.

menu.note: The menu is DATA, not prose in a skill file, so the manager can extend it (ladder rung 3). Adding a domain or a kind here is a legitimate strategic move.

kinds.name: New element
kinds.what: a thing the town did not contain

kinds.name: New CA rule
kinds.what: a new per-cell rule that makes the grid evolve

kinds.name: Deepen
kinds.what: make an existing system richer, or wire two together

kinds.name: Connect
kinds.what: link two places or systems that ignore each other

kinds.name: Polish
kinds.what: make what is there read better; add nothing

kinds.name: Interaction/UX
kinds.what: how you read, poke or navigate the diorama

kinds.name: Scale/World
kinds.what: change the size, span or time of the world itself

kinds.name: Harness
kinds.what: the loop's own instruments — gates, probes, runlog, stats. Changes nothing a viewer sees, and does NOT count toward a domain's balance

coverage.note: domain -> kind -> iteration numbers. Pre-loop work (CHANGELOG iterations 1-31, hand-driven) is recorded as `pre` so the manager knows the ground it stands on.

inventory.note: What the town ALREADY CONTAINS, in the words a brief would use. Read before you build. The antidote to the previous loop's terminal failure: nine consecutive iterations that each surveyed the world, found everything already existed, and exited.
courtyard: walled garden with an organic bed ring; four arch entrances (two TUNNEL, two SLOT)
planting CA — 11 species, bloom stages, seeds spreading from mature neighbours, crowding and age dieback; rain accelerates every growth term
daisies in the lawn, desire paths from foot wear, benches, a sweeper (05.00-06.30), ivy on the gatehouse
one big courtyard linden (drawTree, CX/CY), sized on maturity(), hard-coded summer green

the beds read the YEAR — growF()/dieF()/bloomCap() off warmth, plus lawn health in groundCol and the ivy. bloomCap is a CEILING, not a kill term; per-cell hardiness holds ~1/7 of cells at the full ceiling, so winter is a scatter of blooms in turned earth rather than an empty grid. probes/beds-year.mjs

Seasonal leaf fall: leafFallF() replaces richness() in the leaves spawner; gust multiplies rather than overrides it; falling leaves take leafCol() so a leaf matches the tree it fell from. R() draw count unchanged.
lane: kiosk (07.30-18.30), pavement cafe with tables, awnings, washing lines, planters, street lamps, benches
market day every 4th day, three stalls, marketActive() 08.00-17.00
washing comes in before the rain — per-garment thresholds, ~1.6 s fades on weatherComing(), plus a dusk ramp; never all in one frame
market put up and packed away — marketRaise(i), a per-stall staggered 0..1 progress (06.90-08.00 up, 17.00-18.10 down) staging trader/trestle/frame/canvas/goods as clamps on it

working day hung off the sun: kioskOpen/marketActive/marketRaise/sweeper/wind announcement are offsets from sunUp/sunDown, neutral at SEASON_START. marketOpen()/marketClose() are the one definition of the market's ends; MK_MIN_SPAN floors winter at 7h, MK_EARLIEST keeps the summer stall-raise inside its own sim day
street: cross street with two footways, roadway, curbs; street lamps; four street trees in stone pits (TREE_PITS, drawLaneTree)
allotment block of 17 plots (buildGrid excludes the pond corner), timber fence, gates, shed, and an alley cut through the block
harvest cycle — harvestPlot() lifts a mature 3x2 bed whole, bAge doubles as a 12-20 s fallow clock, then it is re-sown as a row under plotCrop()
spawnAllotAgent() — the allotments' own arrival source, rate on ripePlots(); ~1.1 gardeners/day, ~1 plot cleared/day; they work 1-3 rows and walk out carrying a basket (a.crop)

Seasonal canopy on all 13 trees (drawTree + drawLaneTree): leafOut/leafFresh/leafDeep/leafTurn/leafShed + leafCol(base,k) — coverage staged as per-blob clamps on one 0..1 progress, bare in winter behind drawBoughs() tapered boughs, thin+light in spring, dark in summer, patchy amber in autumn. All read seasonPhase, not warmth.
Orchard year on the existing fruit:1 flag: blossomF() (white crown, out ahead of the leaves) and fruitF() (apples green->red, gone before the tree is bare)
plaza: plaza with a fountain and a paved roundel, four tree pits, benches
quay along the river with benches

spawnEastAgent() — the east quarter's own arrival source (eastCap/eastRate, a.east, excluded from laneCount, eastOpen() on daylight>0.16); enters by the alley, the quay head or the park gate, visits one stop, leaves the way it came
river: river with a boat, three-arch bridge, towpath, church with tower and nave, bandstand, four orchard trees (drawLaneTree fruit:1), jetty, park gate
pigeons that flush off the belfry when the bell rings, from a finite roost that refills

boatWatch() — anyone byTheWater() (quay and rail, bridge deck, towpath) gets one glance per passing boat (a.watch ~1.4 s, ticked at the top of stepAgent so it never holds anybody); ~2.1 glances per boat
a parapet stop mid-span (PARAPET_Y, PARAPET_Z 1.0), served mainly from spawnEastAgent; somebody is on the bridge ~12% of daylight
sky: day/night cycle (55 s day), sun and moon arc, backdrop hills, wind days, night window lighting, chimney smoke, a balloon

cloudCover() — one slow rate-capped scalar; fronts build over ~half a day and break after rain, rain is gated on it so it never rains from a clear sky, sun and moon veiled, stars put out, drifting banks
weatherComing() — one ramped rain-is-coming predicate off cloudCover(), damped by daylight so overcast nights read 0; three readers at their own trigger points

season() — the YEAR: a cyclic scalar over SEASON_LEN 26 days (~24 real min), phase 0 = midwinter, anchored at 0.25 where warmth = 0.5 and every seasoned term equals the constant it replaced. Rate-capped, continuous through the wrap. TWO sky readers only — day length (dayHours 11.5..17.5 about SOLAR_NOON 12.75; sunUp/sunDown/sunArc/timeLabel) and light (sunVec, the disc's arc and colour, skyCols, roof key). Population breathes only ~15%, floor 7 people. census clock.season

rainFall — a 0..1 shower intensity beside the raining boolean; drops, the overcast tint, pond rings, water sparkle and chimney smoke all read it, so a shower thins out over ~3 s (RAIN_TAIL 2.2 s plus one fall time) instead of cutting
probes/canopy-year.mjs (anchor neutrality, year curve, canopy pixel footprint by suppress-and-diff) and probes/year-strip.mjs (26-day cropped year contact sheet)
life: walkers with itineraries, courtyard and street; eastern itineraries: plaza bench, fountain gaze, quay rail, quay bench, towpath, church green, allotment plot, bridge parapet
cafe sitters who claim and release a table; market and kiosk browsers
ducks, swans, butterflies, fireflies, birds, one night cat, falling leaves (gated on day>=4 or gusty, and on richness() — not on the season)
a clock that strikes and a church bell that answers it at nine and eighteen from day 2; walkers break stride and look up while it rings (a.listen)
greetPass — two passing within 0.9-1.6 cells may stop, turn and talk (a.greet, chatCool); ~2 conversations a minute
street sitters read the sky (refuse above weatherComing() 0.42, released over 0.55..0.88 off a per-agent a.wary); courtyard sitters excluded. Umbrellas up over 0.62..1.17, so ~30% get caught out

THE DIORAMA IS CLICKABLE and has been since before the loop — a bed takes seeds of a real species, the lawn a daisy, the pond crumbs (ducks converge), the fountain a coin, the river a pebble, paving crumbs (birds land). answersTouch(x,y) is the ONE predicate for 'this cell answers': cursor swaps to pointer on it (46% of the frame), handler guards on it. ONE ticker invitation, once ever, at 8 REAL seconds, cancelled if the viewer clicks first, stood down on ?pause. probes/touch-hint.mjs

the ticker is an ordered queue, not an overwrite — TICK_DWELL 2.5 real s, cap 2, 6 s staleness cut; a follow-on line enqueues only when its antecedent is DISPLAYED, and a line may buy its own dwell (lineDwell)
__entities() carries role, act and watch per person — the seam a behaviour probe reads instead of a bespoke hook

the year is felt in how busy the town is — yearBusy(ex) multiplies the DAYLIGHT term of capacity/laneCap/eastCap only, never their fixed share, so the anchor and every night are provably unchanged; read off daySpan() (day length 0..1), not warmth. Exposure differs by source: EX_COURT 0.5 (walled), EX_LANE 1.0, EX_EAST 1.25. eastCap keeps Math.min(7,…) for c10 — summer reaches the ceiling earlier, never raises it. Folded 2-year summer:winter ratio 1.09 -> 1.56 total (courtyard 1.26, lane 1.94, east 2.10), settled mean unchanged at ~21.5. POP_FLOOR 8 + scarcity: a lift on the three arrival RATES only, never the caps, holding the absolute floor at 8 people. probes/season-year.mjs now reports population per arrival source

PAVING + pavingAt(x,y) — the ONE predicate naming which paving a SIDE/ROAD cell is: lane, bridge deck, cross street, plaza mouth, quay, towpath. Each entry carries its own crumbs line AND the box its birds land in, so the words and the birds cannot disagree. crumbSpot() staggers the three birds at thirds of the place's long axis (never under 3 cells) and fits the scatter by moving its CENTRE, so a two-cell quay still reads as three. probes/paving-places.mjs (--shot for the eye check)

openCues.note: The town still casts hard sun shadows under full overcast — drawSunMoon veils the disc, but the ~6 SUN[0]/SUN[2] shadow call sites use fixed alphas.
Rain requires daylight>0.15, so a heavy front peaking overnight builds full cover, never rains, and breaks by morning — overcast nights are commoner than rain.
East agents retrace their inbound route exactly, so arrivals sharing a gate walk single-file; would queue if eastCap rose much above 7

Courtyard sitters (picnic, sitter) do not read the sky — only a.street agents do. Their sit is assigned at a waypoint with no route left, so refusing it would despawn them mid-lawn; extending it inland needs routeToExit() on refusal.
byTheWater() names the three places a person can see the river, and only boatWatch reads it. Any future river event (a swan taking off, ice, a barge) should read that predicate, not re-derive it.

stepClouds' heavy-front probability reads richness(), which pins at day 16 — WEATHER IS THE LAST SLOW SYSTEM STILL ON A ONE-WAY RAMP. season() is available to it. Strongest cue on the board; next batch unless something displaces it.

The allotments inherit bloomCap through the shared caTick path, so crops do not ripen in deep winter, harvestPlot stops and ripePlots()->0 damps their arrival source for ~a fifth of the year. Seasonally true and UNMEASURED — nobody has checked the gardeners come back at the right rate in spring.

The census ladder holds season fixed but still varies the HOUR (21.27/14.73/21.27), so day-gated systems sample unevenly. Fixing hour AND season needs t = 0 or 27.5 (mod 55) — exactly two hours exist, 06.00 and 18.00, both awkward (dawn is empty; 18.00 is inside market pack-down and the bell). A real trade, derived at #16 — do not re-derive.

motion.mjs watches rain as a POPULATION (census life.raindrops), not per drop: raindrops are screen-space and absent from __entities(). A drop that goes NaN or strobes is still invisible; needs one line in __entities() plus a screen-space exemption from motion.mjs's world-bounds test.

#16's census ladder change is a step in the published growth curve: planted 4782 -> 6109 between #15 and #16 with no town change behind it. census-history.jsonl now carries a 'ladder' field; stats.html plots RUNLOG census scalars and knows nothing about it.

maturity() still sizes all 13 trees off a ramp pinned at day 8 — a tree is the same size in its first winter as its fifth. Left alone on purpose (b16 forbade seasonal size); leafOut is now the seam that would make a slow multi-year growth term read as growth rather than glitch.
context-budget printed OVER at the start of #17 (48.8 KB vs 46 KB cap: LEDGER 15.9, SKILL 11.8, LAWS 9.4, state 9.4) and #17's ledger entry makes it worse. Distil this pass.

the sim day rolls at hour 6.00, so any window a seasonal variable drags below 6.00 evaluates against the PREVIOUS day and its day-derived predicates go false mid-window; MK_EARLIEST clamps the market for exactly this reason and nothing else is currently near the seam

eastCap now sits at its 7-person ceiling for materially more of a summer day; the ceiling is unchanged so c10 is no worse per instant, but it is exposed for longer and nobody has watched a summer afternoon at the park gate for the single-file retrace reading as a queue

scarcity (POP_FLOOR rail) also fires in the first sim minute when the town is legitimately empty, so the opening fill is hurried vs HEAD (day 4 mid-morning 13 -> 18 people). maturity() still bounds it, but minute one is now a servo rather than a ramp
context-budget printed OVER at 53.6 KB against a 46 KB cap at the start of #19 (worse than c38's 48.8): LEDGER 18.9, SKILL 11.8, state 11.4, LAWS 9.4. Rotation is overdue.

answersTouch() does not answer PATH, so the plaza roundel around the fountain and the whole courtyard path ring are dead to cursor and click. PAVING.plaza only fires on the plaza's 6x4 MOUTH onto the lane — 24 of the world's 2903 paved cells. Extending the surface to PATH is a real vector but moves the cursor's 46% share and needs touch-hint.mjs re-measured.

watch.note: The whole east half is fed by a single spawnLaneAgent roll under one laneCap. Anything you add out there competes for that one budget — check whether your feature needs its own before you conclude nobody uses it. The bands, measured: cross-street diversion 0.30 of all spawns, then market 0.24, kiosk 0.18, café 0.26, allotment to 0.48, plaza to 0.48, quay 0.48-0.53, green 0.53-0.58. laneCap peaks at 9 in full daylight.

The year (#12) has TWO readers in the sky and one in the courtyard beds. Everything else — the trees, the working hours, the population caps, the weather fronts, the river — still runs on a constant or a one-way ramp. Before briefing anything, ask whether it should read warmth. Same question for cloudCover(), which still has one reader through weatherComing().
